sections.title: Test coverage analysis
sections.content:
Ran real coverage (`bun test --coverage`), not just a read of the truncated snippets. Result: **9 of the 10 files in the provided context are genuinely at 100% line/function coverage.** `format.ts`, `ranking.ts`, `incident-format.ts`, `decisions-shared.ts`, `design-memory-shared.ts`, `ship-format.ts`, `graph-visual.ts`, `FigmaEmbed.ts`, `ResearchActivity.tsx` are solid — including the branch-y edge cases (timeout/reject paths on `withTimeout`, the full tie-break chain in `compareOpportunities`, malformed-timestamp guards). No action needed there.

**The one real gap — and it's a significant one — is `src/components/cadence/Sketch.tsx`.**

```
src/components/cadence/Sketch.tsx | 72.73 % funcs | 15.46 % lines | uncovered: 69-148, 157-222, 272-453
```

Those three uncovered ranges are exactly `SketchLine`, `SketchBar`, and `SketchBarChart` — the three exported React components. The pure helpers (`mulberry32`, `seedOf`, `sketchPath`, `capFirst`, `barInsight`) are well tested across three files.

sections.title: Root cause (the actual finding, not just the symptom)
sections.content:
`src/components/cadence/__tests__/sketch-components.test.tsx` looks like a thorough 1,400-line component suite (~150 assertions) covering exactly these three components. But it never calls the real components. It re-implements their `useMemo` bodies as local functions (`computeSketchLine`, `computeSketchBar`) and rebuilds their JSX trees by hand (`buildSketchLine`, `buildSketchBar`, `buildSketchBarChart`), then asserts against the *copy*. The real `SketchLine`/`SketchBar`/`SketchBarChart` are imported only so the module loads — never invoked. Coverage confirms it: 0% of their lines execute.

I traced why this pattern exists (it's not accidental — it's the same workaround used in `RoomCard.test.tsx` and `Primitives.test.tsx`, and it's why `graph-slider-component.test.tsx` is entirely `it.todo()` stubs):

- `@testing-library/react` and `@testing-library/user-event` are declared in `package.json` and `bun.lock`, but **not installed** — `node_modules/@testing-library` doesn't exist. `render()` throws `Cannot find module`.
- There is also **no DOM at all** in the test process — `document is not defined` even via plain `react-dom/client` + `act()`. No `happy-dom`, `jsdom`, or `GlobalRegistrator` is wired into `test/setup.ts`, despite its comment claiming "Bun has built-in DOM support via WebKit." That comment doesn't hold for this Bun version/config as currently set up.

Net effect: any component using `useState`/`useMemo` (hooks require a React dispatcher, which only exists during a real render) cannot be tested at all right now except by the hand-mirroring trick — which drifts from the real implementation silently and reports fake coverage. If `SketchLine`'s real `useMemo` body ever diverges from `computeSketchLine`'s copy, or the hover `onMouseEnter`/`onFocus` wiring breaks, these 150 tests would keep passing.

sections.title: Fix, in order
What I did *not* flag as a gap
sections.content: `moat-vis.ts` showed 14% coverage in my first scoped run — that's an artifact of not including its own test file in that run, not a real gap; re-running with `moat-vis.test.ts` confirms genuine 100%. Ruled it out rather than reporting a false positive.

sections.title: Priority
sections.content:
1. Register `happy-dom` + run `bun install` (root cause, ~10 min).
2. Replace the mirror-logic tests in `sketch-components.test.tsx` with real `render()` tests (skeletons above cover the shape; port the existing assertions over since the intent/values are already correct, just wire them to real components).
3. Fill in `graph-slider-component.test.tsx`'s `it.todo()` list the same way.

codeBlocks.code:
bun add -d happy-dom @happy-dom/global-registrator
bun install   # materializes the already-declared @testing-library/react + user-event
